Task: List five surprising facts about the Roman Empire.

• The ancient Romans had concrete that could set and harden underwater, thanks to a mix containing volcanic ash; some of their harbor structures are still intact after two millennia.  
• For more than 200 years, from 27 BCE to 180 CE, the Empire experienced the Pax Romana—an era of relative peace and prosperity—despite governing up to one-fifth of the world’s population.  
• Romans used a postal service (the cursus publicus) that could relay messages across 50 km or more per day, enabling directives from Rome to reach Britain or Egypt in roughly a week.  
• The city of Rome hosted a fire-fighting brigade of thousands—created by Marcus Licinius Crassus and later made public by Emperor Augustus—centuries before many modern cities adopted organized fire services.  
• Some emperors instituted edible money substitutes during coin shortages; for example, during festivities, Trajan reportedly distributed flat bread stamped to resemble coins, redeemable later for actual currency or goods.

Time taken: 16 seconds.
